title: Optimized protocol for immunophenotyping of melanoma and tumor-bearing skin from mouse
protocol: Shave mice prior to harvesting skin or tumor.
Cut skin tumors into thin strips and then into 1-2 mm² squares.
Digest tissues using Collagenase P for optimal cell viability and counts.
Incubate tissues in digestion enzyme mixture at 4°C for 16-20 hours.
Do not include a red blood cell (RBC) lysis buffer to avoid decreasing cell viability.
Use fixation and permeabilization reagents that lyse RBCs for intracellular protein detection.
Euthanize mice according to institutional guidelines, typically by sedation with 5% isoflurane, followed by asphyxiation and physical confirmation of death by cervical dislocation.
Shave fur from tumor sites and peripheral area.
Harvest tumors using scissors and forceps.
Place tumors in cold PBS.
Place tumors in 10cm dishes on ice.
Cut tumors into strips.
Cut strips into 1–2 mm² squares.
Place tumors squares into a 6-well plate and add 5 mL digestion media.
Incubate the plate containing tumor squares on a rocker in a cold room for 16–20 h.
Place tumors and digestion media through a 70 μM cell strainer.
Use a 3 ml or 5 ml syringe plunger to mash the tumor on the strainer and wash the strainer twice with DMEM containing 5% FBS.
Filter the tumor and media through a 50μM cell strainer.
Wash and count cells with Trypan Blue and a hemocytometer.
Shave off any hair from the tumor and peripheral area.
Cut the tumor around the periphery, minimizing non-tumor bearing skin.
Harvest the tumor bearing skin and weigh it.
Place the tumor in a 50 mL conical tube containing FACS buffer.
Store the tube at 4°C for up to 1 month.
Place the tube on ice and work on the next mouse.
Cut the tumor into small strips on a 100 mm dish on ice.
From the strips, cut the tumor into approximately 1–2 mm² squares.
Cut tumor into strips and squares.
Place cut tumor in a 6-well plate with 5 mL tumor digestion media.
Store the 6-well plate at 4°C.
Place the 6-well plate on a rocker in a cold room for 16–20 hours.
Transfer the contents of each well to an individual 50 mL conical tube overlaid with a 70 μM cell strainer.
Add 2 mL DMEM with 10% FBS to the wells to collect any remaining single cells and transfer to the same cell strainer.
Use a 5 mL syringe plunger to further crush tissue pieces on the 70 μM strainer, three times.
Rinse the cell strainer with 5 mL DMEM plus 10% FBS between each tissue crush.
Place the 50 mL conical tube in an ice box while working on the next samples.
Centrifuge the 50 mL tubes at 450 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 5 mL DMEM containing 10% FBS.
Transfer the resuspended contents to a 15 mL conical tube containing a 50 μM cell strainer.
Place the tubes in a centrifuge and spin at 450 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL DMEM containing 10% FBS.
Count cells using a hemocytometer and trypan blue.
Prepare antibody lineage cocktail in FACS buffer.
Add ILC2 extracellular surface antibodies to the cocktail.
Prepare the GATA3 antibody dilution in FACS buffer in a separate tube for intracellular staining.
Aliquot 2–4 million cells per sample per well in a 96-well plate for staining with the ILC2 extracellular surface antibody cocktail.
Wash cells with cold 1× DPBS to remove DMEM at 450 g at 4°C for 5 min.
Decant the supernatant in a quick downward motion.
In the dark, add 50 μL of 1/2000 viability dye to each well, except to the unstained control well.
Incubate for 30 min on ice in the dark.
Add 100 μL cold 1× DPBS to each well.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant in a quick downward motion.
Add 10 μL of Fc receptor blocking reagent to each well.
Incubate for 30 min on ice in the dark.
Without washing the plate, add 25 μL of the ILC2 antibody cocktail directly to the wells.
Incubate for 30 min on ice in the dark.
Add 100 μL cold FACS buffer to each well.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant in a quick downward motion.
Add 100 μL of FOXP3 Fixation/Permeabilization solution (1:4 dilution with Fixation/Permeabilization Diluent) to each well.
Incubate for 30 min on ice in the dark.
Add 100 μL cold 1× permeabilization buffer to each well.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant in a quick downward motion.
Add 10 μL of Fc receptor blocking reagent to each well.
Incubate for 30 min on ice in the dark.
Without washing the plate, add 50 μL of the diluted GATA3 antibody directly to the wells.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C) in the dark.
Add 150 μL cold 1× permeabilization buffer to each well.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant in a quick downward motion.
Resuspend in 150 μL cold 1× permeabilization buffer to each well.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C) in the dark.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant in a quick downward motion.
Resuspend in 200 μL cold 1× FACS buffer to each well.
Wrap plate in aluminum foil to protect from light and keep at 4°C.
Acquire single cells from the digested tumor.
Characterize T-cells and myeloid cells by flow cytometry using specific markers.
Identify CD3+ cells, CD4+ T-cells, CD8+ T-cells, regulatory T-cells (Tregs).
Distinguish monocytic-myeloid-derived suppressor cells (M-MDSCs) and granulocytic-MDSCs (G-MDSCs).
Identify non-lymphoid tissue dendritic cells.
Characterize myeloid dendritic cells.
Differentiate macrophages using flow cytometry markers.
Use Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) controls for proper gating.
Apply isotype controls for accurate analysis.
Include an unstained control for precise gating.
Utilize lineage markers to discriminate ILC2s.

Take the plate out of the fridge.
Transfer samples to individual 5 mL FACS tubes.
Prepare compensation tubes with each fluorochrome listed above.
Perform acquisition using BD LSRFortessa.
Ensure there is enough sheath fluid in the tank.
Ensure the waste tank is not full.
Create a new data acquisition matrix using BD FACSDiva or available software.
Select all forward scatter and side scatter parameters (Area, Height, Width).
Assign each channel to fluorochromes and delete the rest.
Prime the instrument twice to remove debris.
Perform Cytometer Setup and Tracking (CST) if required by the core facility for the first user of the day.
Use the unstained control to set voltages for FSC-A, SSC-A, and fluorochromes.
Right-click on Cytometer Settings → Application Settings → Create Worksheet.
Draw a gate around the lymphocyte population in the SSC-A and FSC-A plot.
Ensure the negative population is on the “+” sign in plots showing fluorochromes.
Perform compensation using your compensation tubes.
Set an interval gate for the negative population peak.
Move the P2 gate on the positive population peak.
Calculate compensation.
Click “Link & Save”.
Click on the little sheet icon to get back to the analysis schematic and set up gating strategy.
Acquire all samples, including FMO and unstained controls.
Ensure the threshold rate is at 10,000 events/second during acquisition.
Export data according to core facility guidelines in FCS3.0 format for BD FlowJo analysis.
Perform cleaning and shutdown procedures according to your institute’s core facility guidelines.
Acquire all stained cells in the tube without setting a predetermined number of events.
Normalize acquired ILC2s to CD45+ cells or as an absolute number from total cell count, tissue weight, and total cells acquired via FACSDiva.
Adjust acquisition range for ILC2s based on days post-4-HT induction: approximately 10,000–40,000 ILC2s per 1 million CD45+ cells at Day 7.
At Day 14, the range is approximately 3,000–60,000 ILC2s per 1 million CD45+ cells.
For Day 40, acquire from 4,000–15,000 ILC2s per 1 million CD45+ cells.
